PullRequest.Title: chat: enforce strict marketplaces only from managed settings

Fixes #341657

## Changes

- Remove `chat.plugins.strictMarketplaces` entirely, including its `ChatStrictMarketplaces` policy projection, catalog entry, readiness metadata, and obsolete policy telemetry fields. No migration, alias, or hidden fallback; stale user values are ignored.
- Read `strictKnownMarketplaces` through `IManagedSettingsService`. Keep native MDM watching the key without a configuration registration, preserving native MDM > server > file delivery and live updates/removal.
- Route marketplace trust, discovery, public-feed availability, picker labels, and in-flight cancellation through the marketplace service. Remove the install notification's link to the deleted setting.
- Preserve managed empty-array lockdown and allowlist restrictions on **both** user-added and enterprise-added marketplaces. Already-installed plugins are not retroactively disabled.
- Add regression coverage for stale values, managed additions, allowlists/lockdown, all three managed delivery channels, picker attribution, and live query/update behavior. Update the managed-settings guide.

## Validation

Validated on Windows with Node 24.18.0, including a successful rebase onto current `main`.

- `npm.cmd run build-fast -- --client-only` — passed.
- `npm.cmd run typecheck-client` — passed.
- Targeted ESLint on all 26 changed TypeScript files — passed; final test adjustments were re-linted successfully.
- `npm.cmd run export-policy-data` — passed for both workbench entrypoints; generated catalog removes only the retired policy.
- `node --test build\lib\test\policyConversion.test.ts` — 12 passed.
- Focused Electron unit tests below — **574 passed**, including after rebasing.

Dependency restoration initially hit a registry-proxy 404; installing the same pinned dependencies from the official npm registry with the existing Windows build prerequisites resolved it. No dependency manifests were changed. Full smoke/integration suites, live enterprise MDM/provider flows, manual UI/screen-reader checks, and cross-platform runs were not performed.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed JSON.parse, all callers, per-reference filtering, and catalog query source reconstruction are directly traced. Exact milliseconds depend on enterprise allowlist and marketplace counts, so severity is low, but the repeated serialization/allocation mechanism and UI-path multiplicity are certain.
Findings.PerformanceResource: CPU work and temporary arrays/objects from JSON.parse and allowlist filtering
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For N configured marketplaces and an M-entry managed allowlist, source construction invokes this decoder roughly twice per marketplace (plus additional policy checks), so decoding/allocation grows O(N*M) per catalog query; malformed JSON also throws and logs on every invocation.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Increased synchronous search/picker latency and avoidable GC pressure; malformed managed values additionally cause repeated exception and log I/O.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: The deleted configuration-backed path called getStrictKnownMarketplaces on configurationService.getValue(ChatConfiguration.StrictMarketplaces), which supplied the already-decoded array from the typed array policy setting, so trust checks did not JSON.parse the whole managed payload.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new _getStrictMarketplaces reads the raw JSON string and parses and validates it on every isStrictMarketplacePolicyActive/isMarketplaceTrusted call.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: RIGHT line 854 adds JSON.parse(value) inside _getStrictMarketplaces, and the same diff changes both trust methods to call this helper instead of consuming the configuration service's decoded array.
Findings.Title: Cache the decoded strict-marketplace allowlist
Findings.Impact: Opening or searching the customization marketplace rebuilds sources: CustomizationMarketplaceWorkbenchService.sources and getService call getMarketplaceReferences, whose per-reference filter calls isStrictMarketplacePolicyActive and then isMarketplaceTrusted. With several configured marketplaces and a nontrivial enterprise allowlist, one debounced search repeatedly decodes the same payload many times on the UI path; an invalid native/server/file value also emits the warning repeatedly.
Findings.Evidence: CustomizationMarketplaceWorkbenchService.query reads this.sources, then getService rebuilds provider descriptors; both paths call getMarketplaceReferences. getMarketplaceReferences filters every configured reference through _isMarketplaceAllowedByStrictPolicy, which calls isStrictMarketplacePolicyActive and, when active, isMarketplaceTrusted, and both call _getStrictMarketplaces. The added JSON.parse therefore runs repeatedly for the same immutable managed value within one query. The managed-settings observable already identifies value changes, providing a natural invalidation point.
Findings.Recommendation: Decode and validate the raw value once when strictMarketplaces changes (or memoize by raw string), cache the resulting allowlist, and log malformed JSON once per distinct value; have both policy/trust methods read that cached result.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open, browse, search, or paginate the AI customization marketplace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Synchronous source construction and strict-policy filtering complete before the catalog request is issued; then selected provider/network results are awaited before rendering. The newly added cancellation listener is bookkeeping on this critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Query harness/public-feed, platform marketplace sources, and fetch configured GitHub marketplace definitions
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One logical query fans out through the existing selected sources; plugin work is once per deduplicated configured marketplace, with warm GitHub cache hits avoiding HTTP.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same marketplace/provider queries and per-marketplace fetches occurred before the diff; the diff changes policy filtering and cancellation, not boundary count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Catalog rendering awaits the selected source queries.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Effective configured marketplace references after canonical-ID deduplication, managed allowlist entries, selected sources, and catalog pages; search is debounced by 300 ms.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Configured marketplace fetches use the existing Promise.all fan-out across deduplicated references; source providers are queried by the existing marketplace service. The PR adds cancellation/coherence but no limiter or new remote operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: GitHub marketplace data uses the existing persisted TTL cache; cloned repositories use the existing repository cache/refresh age. Continuation pages reuse in-memory query state. The managed allowlist itself is not cached after decoding, which is the reported issue.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: source getter, query, trust-check, cache, and network call paths were inspected directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical enterprise allowlist and configured-marketplace counts are unknown, so the repeated JSON decoding finding is low severity; network cardinality is established and unchanged.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable synchronous repeated serialization/allocation was introduced; no new network fan-out was introduced.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply, update, or remove strictKnownMarketplaces through native MDM, server, or file delivery while marketplace work is active
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Channel resolution updates the managed-settings bag, the strict-value observable invalidates marketplace queries, active relevant queries/installations are cancelled, and update checks may be rescheduled immediately. Cancellation is on the active operation path; subsequent refresh is driven by existing consumers.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Watch native managed-settings definitions and receive native policy updates
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One existing watcher subscription containing one additional key, not one watcher or IPC call per key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The watcher already existed and watched the aggregate definitions; the diff adds strictKnownMarketplaces to the same payload rather than creating a new boundary.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Watcher initialization is part of managed-settings startup; live callbacks update in-memory state.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Fetch/check each unique allowed installed marketplace during an immediate update check after a real strict-policy change
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one fetch per unique allowed marketplace represented by installed plugins, processed sequentially.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Changing the former strict configuration already cleared update state and scheduled the same immediate update check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Off the direct settings-update UI critical path, but consumes background network/repository work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing channel-level refresh, independent of marketplace count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: File managed-settings delivery already read and resolved the bag; this diff only consumes another key.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to resolve file policy before firing the in-memory change.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One effective strict setting after native MDM > server > file precedence, active in-flight queries/installations, and unique marketplaces represented by installed plugins.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Managed-setting updates are deduplicated by bag equality and strict raw-string equality. Update checks remain one scheduled run and fetch unique installed marketplaces sequentially; query cancellation coalesces through existing UI refresh scheduling.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Unchanged strict strings do not emit through the observable. Query continuations are invalidated on a real marketplace change. Update checks use existing repository state and GitHub cache behavior; failures are not newly retried by this diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: equality checks, observable equality, cancellation ownership, and update scheduling were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The frequency of enterprise live-policy changes and number of active operations is deployment-specific; event deduplication and existing scheduling bound the mechanism.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional boundary fan-out or concurrency burst was introduced; cancellation stores are disposed on completion. Repeated decoding of the delivered value is covered by the submitted finding.

Scenarios.Scenario: Install, repair, or update a marketplace customization while source policy changes
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Trust/source validation precedes provider install, repository/network fetch, or filesystem mutation. New source-change listeners can cancel the operation before completion and are disposed with the per-operation store.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Provider install, marketplace fetch, repository pull, connector operation, or package/git update
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One provider/install path per coalesced resource; update-all performs one pull per unique marketplace plus existing per-plugin work.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same install/update boundaries existed; the diff adds policy-aware cancellation and removes a settings action.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist installation records and inspect/update plugin source directories
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing per installation/update record and source operations.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One coalesced pending operation per customization key; update-all groups marketplace pulls by canonical marketplace before per-plugin updates.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Duplicate installs remain coalesced by the pending map. Update-all keeps existing per-marketplace/per-plugin Promise.all behavior. The added listeners do not launch work and cancellation is per active operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configured-plugin resolution uses existing marketplace caches unless refresh is requested; policy changes invalidate relevant queries but do not add an installation cache.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: listener lifecycle, pending-operation coalescing, and transitive install/update calls were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider-specific install duration varies, but no new expensive operation is launched by the changed listeners.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression beyond the shared repeated allowlist decoding; cleanup and concurrency remain bounded.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open and interact with the Manage Plugin Marketplaces picker
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Configured references, labels, and policy eligibility are built synchronously before the picker is shown. Filesystem existence is checked only after one marketplace is selected.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check whether the selected marketplace repository directory exists
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one check after selecting a marketplace.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same existence check was already present.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Delays showing the selected marketplace's action picker.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Deduplicated configured marketplace count and strict allowlist length.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Picker item construction is synchronous; the post-selection filesystem check is one awaited operation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Configuration parsing is repeated as before. The new raw managed allowlist is re-decoded per policy/trust check instead of cached, as reported.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the picker loop and post-selection boundary were inspected.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Most users configure few marketplaces, limiting impact; larger managed deployments increase synchronous decode/match work.
Scenarios.Verdict: The changed eligibility source is correct from a boundary perspective, but its per-item raw JSON decoding is the submitted low-severity regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Workbench startup and periodic plugin marketplace update checks
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Native managed-settings watcher setup and installed-plugin metadata hydration occur during service initialization/idle work; periodic update checks are scheduled after global idle and are off the immediate startup rendering path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Create the aggregate native policy watcher
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One watcher at startup regardless of key count; this diff adds one definition to its payload.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same aggregate watcher was created before.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Part of managed-settings initialization, with no extra round trip per added key evidenced.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Hydrate installed plugin metadata from repositories/manifests
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per unhydrated installed entry, with repository reads shared according to existing repository behavior.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Background observable hydration, not newly moved onto startup UI rendering.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check unique allowed installed marketplaces for updates
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential fetch per unique allowed marketplace per scheduled interval or real policy change.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same scheduling and boundary cardinality under the former strict configuration.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of watched managed keys, unhydrated installed plugins, and unique marketplaces among installed plugins.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: One native watcher is created for all definitions. Metadata hydration processes entries sequentially. Periodic update checks are serialized by the existing delayer/running flag.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Installed metadata and repository/GitHub caches are existing. A real strict-policy change clears update availability and reschedules one check; unchanged values are deduplicated.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for lifecycle and cardinality; native-module internal per-key setup cost is not visible and is not sufficient for a finding.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Native watcher implementation cost per extra definition is not measured, but the boundary remains one aggregate subscription and no scaling regression is evidenced.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable startup, cache-lifecycle, or concurrency regression.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 28 changed files. One low-severity repeated serialization/allocation regression was submitted for reparsing the raw strict-marketplace allowlist on every policy/trust check. Managed-update deduplication, query/install cancellation cleanup, native watcher aggregation, marketplace boundary cardinality, cache behavior, and update-check concurrency otherwise remain bounded or unchanged.
